newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - April 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - April 1.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Brisbane Broncos remain undefeated in Super League after their tough 14-12 victory over the Cronulla Sharks at the ANZ Stadium yesterday. Brisbane trailed for most of the match but Darren Smith scored the winning try in the 65th minute. Page 26.

Sydney United defeated Collingwood 3-2 in the national soccer league with David Zdrilic scoring a late goal for United. Only 450 supporters watched the match, which keeps United on track for the minor premiership. Page 24.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The AJC Sires Produce Stakes at Randwick yesterday was won by the Clarrie Conners trained Encounter, ridden by Shane Dye. Dye begins a five-meeting suspension today, while Conners has now trained three Sires' winners from the same family. Page 38.

The three Australian Super Twelve rugby union sides will all play home games this weekend, as Australia tries to gain ground on the other nations competing in the tournament. Queensland yesterday suffered their fifth loss in a row, falling 49-26 to Aucklnd at Eden Park, Queensland. Page 37.

The NSW Rugby Union has been accused of making a stupid mistake in predicting a reduction in the number of teams in the first grade competition from 14 to 12. Their proposal to introduce a world club tournament in Australia has been seen, however, as a wecome move. Page 36.
THE AGE

Carlton AFL coach David Parkin has requested the league to monitor the deliberate time-wasting of players near the end of matches. Parkin claims the tactic is influencing the result of games and can result in the game being labelled a farce. Page B8.

Daniel Millard won the Stawell Gift foot race yesterday as he repeated the performance of his great-grandfather, William Millard, who won in 1878. Millard yesterday collected $30,000 after almost withdrawing due to a bad handicap. Page B8.

Matt Hoy yesterday won the Rip Curl Pro surfing tournament at Bells Beach against Damien Hardman in a 1.5 metre surf. The Newcastle surfer won the year's third tournament and is now second in the world rankings to American Kelly Slater. Page B6.
THE HERALD SUN

Carlton AFL player Greg Williams may be on report after pushing an umpire in yesterday's game against Essendon. Essendon won the game 106 to 99 in front of a crowd of 82,363 at the Melbourne Cricket Ground. Page 80.

Geelong full-forward Gary Ablett has been cleared of serious damage to his right knee and will return to the senior grade this weekend. Ablett jarred his knee in a reserves game against Richmond last weekend, where he scored seven goals. Page 73.

In the final of the women's basketball league pre-season competition, the Sydney Casino Flames have defeated the Melbourne Tigers 64-58. Melbourne coach Ron Tomlinson was optimistic about the loss and has predicted a successful year for his team. Page 71
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

North Queensland captain Steve Walters has been sent off for an alleged kneeing incident, as North Queensland defeated the Canterbury Bulldogs 16-14 at Belmore Sports Ground. It was Canterbury's second successive defeat and only the Cowboy's second win for the season. Page 60.

Star Sydney Swans full-forward Tony Lockett will not return from injury until round three after off-season groin surgery. Defender Paul Roos will miss at least one week after twisting a knee and Mark Baytes will be absent for a fortnight with a strained amstring. Page 58.

Newcastle ARL player Paul Harragon has been cleared to play after migraine concerns and will return in a fortnight. After suffering severe headaches earlier in the season, he was banned from playing for a month. Page 54.
